focus: 擋回不合理時程與臨時插件
lead: 今天練的是當日期不是你訂的、需求卻塞到你頭上時怎麼談。心法：不要爭論「合不合理」，改成把代價算成數字攤在桌上，然後把選擇權還給對方。每個 speaking 段落請先出聲講完再看 model answer。

phrases.en: Let's separate the ask from the date.
phrases.gl: 先把「要做什麼」跟「什麼時候要」拆開談（一拆開，八成的僵局就解了）
phrases.ex: Let's separate the ask from the date — I'm not arguing about the demo, I'm arguing about the 25th.

phrases.en: If we do that, the first thing that breaks is…
phrases.gl: 如果照你說的做，第一個垮掉的會是 ——（用後果代替拒絕）
phrases.ex: If we do that, the first thing that breaks is night collection — those two cars are the only ones with the calibrated night rig.

phrases.en: I can give you X, but not Y.
phrases.gl: 我可以給你 X，但給不了 Y（先給再收，對方比較聽得進去）
phrases.ex: I can give you one car for the full three weeks, but not two.

phrases.en: That date was set without the delivery team in the room.
phrases.gl: 這個日期訂的時候我們不在場（陳述事實，不是抱怨，也不指責個人）
phrases.ex: That date was set without the delivery team in the room, so let me tell you what's actually behind it.

phrases.en: Let's not trade a certain loss for a possible win.
phrases.gl: 不要拿確定的損失去換不確定的收穫（一句話擋掉賭博式決策）
phrases.ex: Pulling the cars off night runs costs us the whole night set — let's not trade a certain loss for a possible win.

phrases.en: Can we agree on the principle first, then the numbers?
phrases.gl: 我們先對原則，再談數字（避免一開始就在細節上卡死）
phrases.ex: Can we agree on the principle first — customer-facing demos win over internal milestones — then the numbers?

phrases.en: Let me put a number on that.
phrases.gl: 我把它換算成數字（把「很多」「很趕」變成可以被討論的東西）
phrases.ex: Let me put a number on that: a five-day lens evaluation is two vehicle slots and about a week of Ivy's time.
phrases.fix: 取代 “It's quite a lot of work for us”

phrases.en: I disagree with the sequencing, not the priority.
phrases.gl: 我反對的是順序，不是它的重要性（把爭議縮到最小的那一塊）
phrases.ex: I disagree with the sequencing, not the priority — the fisheye work matters, it just can't go first.
phrases.fix: 取代 “I have different opinion with you”

phrases.en: So where does that leave us?
phrases.gl: 那我們現在的結論是什麼？（談完把對話收斂成決定，不要讓它散掉）
phrases.ex: So where does that leave us — one car to you from Monday, and the demo moves to the 29th?

setup: Setup. It's the Wednesday cross-program resource review. Rachel, who runs the chassis program, needs two of your four test vehicles for the next three weeks to finish brake calibration, and hers is the only program with a hard homologation date. The problem is that those same two cars are the only ones carrying the calibrated night rig, so handing them over stops night collection completely. Separately, Vincent in sales has already told the customer there will be a live night cut-in demo on the 25th — you found out from the customer's calendar invite. And Kevin from hardware wants you to squeeze in a five-day evaluation of a new lens vendor “while the cars are idle anyway.”

prompts.q: Rachel: “I need two of your four cars from Monday, for three weeks. Homologation can't move.”
prompts.frame: Accept her constraint out loud → name what specifically breaks → put a number on it → offer a smaller concrete give → hand the choice back.
prompts.say: 先出聲講完整段（目標 40 秒），不要用 “maybe” 或道歉開場，再看 model answer。
prompts.model: “Your date is real, so I'm not going to argue with it. Here's my problem: those two specific cars are the only ones with the calibrated night rig, so if they go, night collection stops — not slows, stops. That's about eight collection slots, roughly two weeks of night data we can't get back before the September drop. Let me put a number on the alternative: I can give you one car for the full three weeks starting Monday, and the second one for the last week only, once our night set is closed. If that's not enough for you, then the honest answer is one of our two programs slips, and that's a call for David and your side, not for the two of us in this room. Which of those do you want to take upstairs?”

prompts.q: Vincent: “The customer already has the 25th in their calendar for the night cut-in demo. We can't walk that back now.”
prompts.frame: Separate the ask from the date → state plainly that you weren't in the room → give the earliest date you'd actually defend → offer a real fallback for the 25th → ask for the decision.
prompts.say: 出聲練習「對事不對人地擋掉一個既成事實」，語氣平穩不帶情緒。
prompts.model: “Let's separate the ask from the date. I want that demo to happen — a live night cut-in is the strongest thing we have. What I can't do is stand behind the 25th, and that date was set without the delivery team in the room. Right now we have four clean night runs; a demo the customer would find convincing needs closer to ten, and at two slots a week that lands us at the 29th at the earliest. Here's my fallback: on the 25th we show recorded night footage running through the live pipeline, which is honest and still impressive, and we book the in-car demo for the first week of September. What I'd rather not do is put them in a car on the 25th and have it miss a cut-in in front of them. Can you take that back to them today, so I know which one I'm building for?”

prompts.q: Kevin, after the meeting: “The cars are idle at night anyway — can you just squeeze in the five-day lens evaluation?” You have to say no.
prompts.frame: Correct the false premise gently → put a number on the real cost → say no clearly for this window → offer a smaller version with a date → close the loop.
prompts.say: 出聲講一次乾脆的拒絕 —— 不准說 “I will try my best”，也不要用 “sorry” 開場。
prompts.model: “They're not idle — the night runs are exactly when those cars are working hardest, so the free time you're seeing on the calendar is already booked. And let me put a number on the ask: a five-day evaluation is two vehicle slots plus about a week of Ivy's time to redo the extrinsics afterwards, so it's closer to two weeks of impact than five days. So it's a no for this window. What I can do is this: give me the lens spec sheet and we'll run it on the static rig next Tuesday — that gets you distortion and low-light numbers without touching a car. If those look good, I'll put a proper on-road evaluation into the October plan. Send me the spec by Friday and I'll confirm the rig slot Monday.”

fixes.bad: We need approval from customer before we change scope.
fixes.good: We need approval from the customer before we change the scope.
fixes.note: Articles：中文沒有冠詞，所以最容易整句漏掉。特定的人事物（那個客戶、這次的範圍）前面要 the，這是英語母語者第一個會聽出來的破綻。

fixes.bad: I'm not comfortable to commit this date.
fixes.good: I'm not comfortable committing to this date.
fixes.note: Preposition + verb form：be comfortable 後面接 -ing，不接 to V；承諾某件事要用 commit to。這句在協商時很常用，值得整句背下來。

fixes.bad: This request is very big for us, it will impact a lot.
fixes.good: This request adds about two weeks and costs us four vehicle slots.
fixes.note: Vagueness：very big / a lot 沒有給對方任何可以判斷的東西，反而聽起來像在討價還價。換成數字，你的立場立刻變得難以反駁。

fixes.bad: You must give me the answer today, otherwise I cannot start.
fixes.good: I need an answer by five today to hold the slot — can you get back to me?
fixes.note: Register：must 對平行單位講會變成命令，容易踩到人。改成「我需要什麼 + 為什麼 + 具體時間」，壓力一樣在，但關係不會壞。

fixes.bad: If they would agree with our plan, we can start the collection next week.
fixes.good: If they agree with our plan, we can start collection next week.
fixes.note: Conditional：真實條件句的 if 子句用現在式，不放 would（也不放 will）。中文的「如果他們會同意」直譯過來就會多這個字。

challenge:
今天在真實會議裡做這一件事：當有人給你一個你沒參與訂的日期，先拆開再算給他看 ——

“Let's separate the ask from the date. If we do that, the first thing that breaks is ___. Let me put a number on it: ___. I can give you ___, but not ___. So where does that leave us?”

錄音作業（60 秒，手機錄）：挑一個這週真的壓在你身上、但不是你訂的時程，用英文練一次協商。

  • 前 20 秒必須先承認對方的限制是真的（不要一開口就防守）
  • 必須把代價換算成一個數字（幾天、幾台車、幾個 slot）
  • 必須給出一個你真的做得到的較小方案，而且附日期
  • 結尾必須用一句話把討論收成決定（So where does that leave us?）
  • 禁用：very big、a lot、you must、I will try my best
check: 我今天有沒有把「要做什麼」和「什麼時候要」分開來談，而不是整包吵？
我拒絕的時候，有沒有把代價換算成一個具體數字攤在對方面前？
談完之後，我有沒有用一句話把它收成一個決定，而不是讓話題就這樣散掉？
